message.content:
Add a MANAGER-APPROVAL gate to the Soul Pilates "reception review-upload" feature you can find on branch feature/reception-review-uploads. Work in the existing isolated clone at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/soulpilates (a .NET net10.0 + Astro + MongoDB app; totally isolated from any live system).

SETUP:
- `export PATH="/root/.dotnet:$PATH"` (dotnet 10 SDK); node/npm on PATH.
- `export GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -i /root/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new"` for git.
- `cd /tmp/.../scratchpad/soulpilates && git checkout feature/reception-review-uploads && git pull` (this branch has the feature at commit 2791108: ReviewUpload entity, ReviewUploadService, ReviewUploadController, Astro reception-reviews.astro, and a KPI helper `EffectiveGoogleReviewCount(config, metrics) = config.GoogleReviewCount + metrics.ReviewUploadCount` in ReceptionistKpiService.cs).

GUARDRAILS: Work ONLY in that clone. NEVER touch the live box 51.79.226.200 / its Mongo / services. No deploy. Commit + push the SAME branch feature/reception-review-uploads. Keep everything ADDITIVE and DO NOT alter the existing manual GoogleReviewCount path. Compile-verify before finishing: backend `dotnet build -c Release SoulPilates.API/SoulPilates.API.csproj` (0 errors) and frontend `cd SoulPilates.Astro && npm ci && npm run build` (0 errors). (Note: the SoulPilates.Tests project has ~12 PRE-EXISTING build errors from stale test doubles unrelated to this work — don't try to fix those; build the API csproj + Astro, not the whole .slnx.)

THE APPROVAL GATE:
1. Add an approval state to the ReviewUpload entity: `ReviewApprovalStatus` enum { Pending, Approved, Rejected } (default Pending), plus `ApprovedByStaffId string?`, `ApprovedAt DateTime?`, `RejectionReason string?`. New uploads are created as **Pending**.
2. KPI integration: only APPROVED uploads count. Change the month metric so `ReviewUploadCount` (the value fed into `EffectiveGoogleReviewCount`) counts only uploads with status Approved for that year+month. With zero approved uploads, the effective count == the manual value (bonus unchanged). The manager's manual GoogleReviewCount field stays untouched and editable.
3. API (in ReviewUploadController or a small admin addition): manager-only (Admin role) endpoints to `approve` and `reject` (with optional reason) a ReviewUpload, setting status + ApprovedByStaffId (from the JWT staff/admin) + ApprovedAt. List should expose the status; add a manager list of PENDING uploads (optionally filter by month) so the manager can review the images before approving. Keep reception's own list showing each upload's status.
4. Astro UI: a manager/admin approval view — list pending review uploads with the image thumbnail + reviewer/notes + Approve / Reject buttons (reuse the existing reception-reviews page's components/patterns and the media URL). Reception's gallery should now show each upload's status badge (Pending/Approved/Rejected). Match existing UI conventions + role-gating (Admin sees approvals; reception sees her own + statuses).
5. Keep the earlier feature's storage/auth patterns (IMediaStorage, JWT roles) intact.

FINISH: dotnet API build + Astro build both 0 errors; commit + push feature/reception-review-uploads. Report: the schema/enum additions, how the KPI now counts only approved uploads (confirming the manual path + zero-upload case are unchanged), the approve/reject endpoints + roles, the UI changes, and the build results. Do NOT deploy.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. - anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Now I'm mapping out the implementation strategy, starting with the ReviewUpload entity where I'll add an approval status enum with Pending, Approved, and Rejected states, along with fields to track which staff member approved it and when the approval occurred.

For the DTOs, I need to expose the status and approval metadata, plus create a separate request DTO for rejection reasons. The service layer will handle the core approval and rejection logic, plus a method to list all pending reviews across staff members. I also need to update the monthly count logic to filter for only approved reviews, since the KPI service queries the collection directly and will need that status filter applied.

On the controller side, I'm adding admin-only endpoints for approving and rejecting reviews, plus listing pending ones. The tricky part is capturing the approver's staff ID from the JWT—instructors have it, but admins might not, so I'll need to handle that gracefully.

For the UI, I'm deciding between adding an approvals section to the existing reception-reviews page or creating a dedicated admin page. The requirement mentions reusing existing patterns, so I'm leaning toward a new dedicated page that follows the same styling conventions.

I need to make sure the gallery's data transfer object includes a status field so I can render status badges on each tile. I'm also thinking through…

content.text:
Done. The manager-approval gate is implemented, both builds are green, and the work is committed and pushed to `feature/reception-review-uploads` (commit `1678aaa`). No deploy performed.

## What shipped

**Schema / enum additions** (`SoulPilates.Core/Entities/ReviewUpload.cs`)
- New `ReviewApprovalStatus` enum `{ Pending=0, Approved=1, Rejected=2 }`.
- Added to the entity: `Status` (default `Pending`, stored as a Mongo string via `[BsonRepresentation(BsonType.String)]`), `ApprovedByStaffId string?` (ObjectId), `ApprovedAt DateTime?`, `RejectionReason string?`. New uploads keep the default `Pending` — `AddAsync` was not changed, so it inherits Pending.
- DTOs (`ReviewUploadDtos.cs`) now expose `Status` (as string), `ApprovedByStaffId`, `ApprovedAt`, `RejectionReason`, plus new `ReviewRejectRequestDto` and `ReviewPendingListDto`.

**KPI now counts only approved uploads** (`ReceptionistKpiService.cs`)
- The month-metric `ReviewUploadCount` (the value fed into `EffectiveGoogleReviewCount(config, metrics) = config.GoogleReviewCount + metrics.ReviewUploadCount`) now counts documents where `Status == Approved` for that year+month. The `EffectiveGoogleReviewCount` helper and the manual `GoogleReviewCount` field are untouched.
- Confirming the invariants: with zero *approved* uploads `ReviewUploadCount == 0`, so the effective count equals the manual value and the bonus is unchanged; the manager's manual path is never written to and stays editable. `IReviewUploadService.CountForMonthAsync` was likewise narrowed to Approved-only for consistency.

**Approve/reject endpoints + roles** (`ReviewUploadController.cs`, all `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`)
- `GET /api/review-uploads/pending?year=&month=` — manager queue of Pending uploads across all receptionists, optional month filter.
- `POST /api/review-uploads/{id}/approve` and `POST /api/review-uploads/{id}/reject` (optional `{ reason }` body) — set status, `ApprovedByStaffId` (from JWT `staff_id`, falling back to `NameIdentifier`), and `ApprovedAt`; return 404 if the upload is missing. Service uses `FindOneAndUpdate` (returns the updated doc). Reception's existing self-service list/gallery/delete are unchanged and now carry the status.

**UI changes**
- New admin-only page `SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/review-approvals.astro`: pending queue with image thumbnail, receptionist name, reviewer/notes/stars, period, Approve/Reject buttons (reject prompts for an optional reason), lightbox, and a month filter with an "All months" toggle — reusing the reception page's `rev-*` patterns and the media `imageUrl`.
- Reception gallery (`reception-reviews.astro`) now renders a Pending/Approved/Rejected status badge per tile (plus the rejection reason when present).
- `AdminLayout.astro`: new `Review Approvals` nav item gated `data-roles="admin"` (reception's own page keeps `admin,receptionist,headinstructor`).

**Build results**
- Backend: `dotnet build -c Release SoulPilates.API/SoulPilates.API.csproj` → 0 errors (65 pre-existing warnings).
- Frontend: `npm ci && npm run build` → 0 errors, 64 pages built, `dist/admin/review-approvals/index.html` generated.
- Left the SoulPilates.Tests project alone per instructions.

Storage/auth patterns (`IMediaStorage` WebP pipeline, JWT roles) were left intact; all changes are additive.
